title: Granular crediting & tiered fallback brainlog
content:
Topline / problem statement

We need a lightweight, low-friction mechanism to let apps (and end users) opt into different fidelity/cost tradeoffs per session or per request path, and to provide clear crediting semantics and automatic tiered fallbacks when higher-fidelity capacity is unavailable.

Goals (high-level)
- Make it trivial for app teams to declare "credit budgets" for sessions and for individual requests so they can control spend in predictable ways.
- Ensure graceful degradation: when premium/model A is unavailable or would violate latency SLOs, automatically fall back to a configured lower-cost alternative rather than failing.
- Provide transparent accounting: logs + console shows how credits were spent (model, tokens, quantization tier, any compression/eviction used).
- Minimal runtime changes for hosted customers; leverage existing routing + fallback plumbing.

Who benefits
- Consumer-facing products that want subscription tiers (e.g., "Pro users get high-fidelity responses up to X credits/day").
- Marketplaces that need per-call billing at a finer granularity (prompt-level vs. token-level buckets).
- Platform teams who want to limit experimental features' blast radius by allocating small credit budgets.

Sketch: primitives and API surface
- credit_profile (object name in request metadata) — pre-configured profile id on account that maps to budgets and fallback chains (but here in scratchpad we just use names)
- session_budget: integer credits attached to session creation (e.g., 1000 credits).
- request_budget_override: optional credits consumed out of session_budget or separate bucket.
- fidelity_tiers: ["high", "medium", "low"] — each maps to: model_hint, expected_tokens_multiplier, cost_multiplier.
- fallback_chain: ordered list of fidelity_tiers with routing policy e.g., latency-first or cost-first.

Example request metadata (pseudo-JSON in a single header):
{
  "x-redwood-credit-profile": "team-pro-chat",
  "x-redwood-session-budget": "200",
  "x-redwood-request-budget": "20"
}

Server-side interpretation (sketch):
- Look up profile: team-pro-chat -> fidelity_tiers = [high, medium, low]; fallback policy = latency-first; tokens_per_unit = 1
- If the request expects 200 tokens and session budget only has 20 credits left, either: a) decline; b) auto-scale to medium/low fidelity to fit cost (preferred).

User stories (rough)
- As a product manager, I want to pin a "Pro" customer to 1000 session credits/day so that we can guarantee X conversations before hitting throttle.
- As a developer, I want an easy header to attach a session budget, so my front end can decrement budget on user actions and signal the server to fall back when exhausted.
- As an ops on-call, I want fallback events to show in traces (which model was attempted, which fallback used, reason: capacity|latency|cost) so I can debug model performance regressions.
- As a designer, I want to show users an "estimated credit cost" before they submit long generation requests.

Acceptance criteria / telemetry
- Telemetry: events emitted for every decision that consumes credits or triggers a fallback. Fields: session_id, request_id, model_attempted, model_served, tokens_in, tokens_out, credits_deducted, fallback_reason.
- Console: per-account heatmap of credit consumption by route and by model.
- API behavior: if fallback_chain exhausted, return a 4xx with a structured reason and suggested client action (reduce tokens, request cheaper tier).
- Performance: decision path should add <5ms to routing latency in the happy-path (cached profile).

Design notes / UX ideas
- Front-end SDK: helper to estimate credits for a proposed call (taking into account temperature, max_tokens, and chosen fidelity tier). We can model a simple multiplicative cost table for UX estimation.
- On exhaustion: show "Switching to lower fidelity to preserve conversation" vs. a hard throttle — allow app teams to opt-in to either behaviour via profile.
- Visual: small "credit burn" indicator in the conversation header; clickable to open a breakdown (cost per message, credits remaining).

Edge cases & open questions
- Q: How do we map credits to token units precisely across models that have different cost profiles?
  - Idea: maintain a per-model normalization factor (like cost_units_per_token) in the model catalog. Credits are decremented as credits -= tokens * model_cost_factor * fidelity_multiplier.
- Q: What happens if two concurrent requests try to simultaneously consume the last credits?
  - Simplest: optimistic decrement with eventual reconciliation; otherwise perform a tiny atomic check-and-decrement in Redis. Tradeoff latency vs. correctness.
- Q: Should credits be refundable when generation aborted / truncated?
  - Probably yes for client-cancelled. For early stop due to rate-limiting maybe pro-rate. Need policy gated by config.
- Q: How do we surface this to enterprise contracts (Reserved Dedicated customers might want different semantics)?
  - For Dedicated, map credits to capacity units (e.g., slot-hours) and use internal accounting. Expose different SLA-level flags in the profile.

Implementation sketch (phases)
- Phase 0 (MVP): read-only profile + per-request override header. No session-level atomic budget. Implement fallback_chain at routing layer, emit telemetry. UI shows events.
- Phase 1: session budgets with atomic decrement (Redis Lua or single-row SQL update). Front-end SDK helpers to estimate cost. Console: breakdown per route.
- Phase 2: policy editor in Console (create credit_profile, map to account tiers) + experiments: A/B different fallback policies and measure retention/latency/cost.

Experiments & metrics
- Baseline experiment: enable fallback for 20% of traffic for a single product route. Measure reduction in errors, change in average per-session cost, NPS/retention proxy (engagement).
- Metrics to track: credits_consumed_per_session, fallback_rate_by_route, mean_latency_before_and_after_fallback, errors_when_fallback_unavailable, customer-visible "credit estimate mismatch" incidents.

Operational concerns
- Cost accounting must be auditable for billing disputes. Keep raw events immutable for 90 days.
- Thundering herd on atomic decrements — consider burst windows (local client estimation + eventual server enforcement).

Notes to self (todo/parking)
- Follow up with Marco on model_catalog cost_factor implementation (JIRA-INF-4821).
- Ask Priya to prototype a lightweight UI mock for the credit-burn indicator — want one that degrades gracefully on mobile.
- Prototype a small SDK helper function: estimateCredits(max_tokens, temperature, fidelity) in JS. Quick win for developer experience.
- Write a small playbook for support to reconcile "I was charged for" disputes (what logs to pull).

Quick mock API examples (really rough)
- Create profile: POST /v1/accounts/:id/credit_profiles {"id":"team-pro-chat","fallback_chain":["high","medium","low"], "policy":"latency-first"}
- Use profile: curl -H "x-redwood-credit-profile: team-pro-chat" -H "x-redwood-session-budget: 250" -d '{...}' https://api.redwood.ai/generate

Closing thoughts
- This sits nicely with existing fallback/routing mechanisms; the tricky parts are: per-session atomicity and developer UX around credit estimates.
- Keep MVP small: start with server-side fallbacks and telemetry, then layer on atomic budgets and console experiences.

Open questions for sync:
- Which product route should we pick for the living experiment? (Hosting: chat-route vs. single prompt generation).
- Appetite for exposing credits in the billing UI (legal needs to sign off first).
note_summary: Draft PRD sketch for session crediting and tiered fallbacks: primitives, user stories, acceptance criteria, implementation phases, metrics, and open questions. MVP should start with server-side fallback + telemetry before adding atomic budget enforcement and console features.
